items.note: S2.1 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks and restores auxiliary values, and S2.2 names three-element subsets, gather, scatter and scratch wires, but neither gives the map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), h=100, the eight-row schedule or the three-stage composition.

S2.1 alludes to frames letting a gate act pointwise and fixing the endpoint operator, but gives neither the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate, nor D_out S D_in^{-1}.

S2.2 names subspaces from three-element subsets and quotes the line about keeping the dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to N, but states no nested-label property, no L=Ich, no budget Wm-2N+2L and no L/N ratio.

S2.4's method realizes the bit network's edge operators as address shears and S2.2 asserts s<Wm, but the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, the projection assignment and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are absent.
Only S2's motivation that both procedures arise from their own fixed network alludes to it; phase frames C_U, the kernels aI+bX_v, s_c and the C^{tensor m} output are not stated.
S2.2/S2.3 state s<Wm and tau=1-2^{-50}, quoting that the deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}; the source L<N/2, the deficits eta, log m<20 and the conclusion s/W<m^tau are missing.
S2.4.1's 'done in tape order' alludes to the ordered later-field updates of lem:ordered-affine-streams, but no stream operation or its O(V) cost is stated.

S2.4.1 correctly states the lower-triangular times partial-permutation times lower-triangular factorization, but says only 'cost scaling with rank' where the paper gives exactly a interchanges of b-digit fields plus O(V); no derivation (elimination, three-update interchange) is given.

S2.4.2 states O(Ve^tau) for chunks of e digits and S2.3 the recursion of s calls on volume V/W; the row-field condition, the shear H<-H+D on every row, the three-update swap and the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) are not given, so it is not derived.

S2.4 states that two disjoint u-bit address fields of an array of volume V are interchanged in O(Vu^tau), matching lem:chunk-swap; the padding and base-m splitting that extend the power-width case are not shown.
S2's method 'build fixed linear networks with frames ... then recurse' covers the butterfly layers only in general terms; no C-tensor children, s_c child calls or binary changes of basis are stated.
No step concerns packed selected-bit additions, the bad set or its repair by sorting.
S2.5 gives the resulting O(Vd^{lambda'}) and S2.3 the generic recursion, but the layer recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) and the exponent condition on lambda' are not stated.

S2.5 states cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), lambda'<1, for a layer on one bit position of up to d chunks; it omits the normalized kernel H_0, the output Q_p(Hz) with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}, and the exact guard-bit evaluation.

S3/S3.1 give the construction in words (powers of y as roots of unity acting by signed shifts, butterfly layers, retained frequency order) but no omega_t=y^{2r/t}, inverse relation, bit-reversed order, layout L or cost.
S3.2 states signed Kronecker packing into the Harvey-van der Hoeven multiplier with exact products; B_0=2^{4p}, the four products, the returned Q_p(fg/r) and the O(rp log(rp)) cost are missing.

S3 states ring convolution by synthetic transforms and packed products; the shared LB order of the two forward transforms consumed by the opposite transform, the normalization by rM, error and cost are not given, so the sub-steps list ingredients rather than the derivation.
S4.3 says resampling expresses the (prime-length) transform through a power-of-two transform keeping both permutations; the identity RF_s=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A and its hypotheses are absent.

S4.4 states that Bluestein turns the middle transform with its permutation into a cyclic convolution and that retained permutations cancel; no chirp or formula is given, and only R cancels (to (u*v)/S^2) while Q is absorbed.
S4.6 refers to 'compatible parameters' and S0 gives kappa=2^{-182}; none of b, p=6b, d, K, T or the prime choice is stated.
S4.2 states the CRT placement on distinct prime cyclic axes preserving convolution; the map Phi with mu_i, its triangular digit form and cost are absent.
S4's method names the phase twist but not the isomorphism x_d->zeta y or how it links complex and ring convolution.

S4 and its sub-steps follow the paper's chain (radix digits, Phi, resampling, chirp, twist, rescale, round, carry), but omit the two source transforms, the pointwise product, the conjugate transform and the two scales by S that undo (u*v)/S^2.
S4.5 states the error is below 1/2 so rounding is exact; the error chain, p=6b and gamma<=b/4 that make it so are absent.
S4.6 states that with V=Tp=Theta(n) every term of the cost table is within O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}); the margins g_i with min 2kappa and the absorption of log factors are not given.
S1 recalls the Schonhage-Strassen n log n conjecture and the Harvey-van der Hoeven bound, but does not say why an O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) bound refutes an eventual lower bound.

errors.paper: Only the source permutation R cancels, giving (u*v)/S^2 in eq:source-permutation-cancel; the target permutation Q is absorbed into the chirp convolution QF_t u = conj(a).(a*(conj(a).u))/T and never cancelled.

errors.says: address shears are done in tape order at cost scaling with rank
errors.paper: The shear by a rank-a matrix costs exactly a interchanges of b-digit fields (each a recursive call) plus O(V) linear work; the cost is not proportional to rank.

chain: The tree follows the paper's top-level route (fast interchange and fast butterfly layers from fixed networks with frames and a rank saving s<Wm, synthetic-transform convolution, then the reduction pipeline and cost table), so it reaches the main bound in outline. It thins out at the core: S2.1-S2.3 assert s<Wm and tau=1-2^{-50} without the labels, the budget Wm-2N+2L, L<N/2 or the endpoint identity, the complex side collapses to the single infer S2.5, and the multiplication pipeline omits the source transforms and S^2 rescaling.

steps.note: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks and restoring auxiliary values is named, but h=100, the triple indexing, N, m and the signed map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) are missing.
Frames are said to let gates act pointwise with the endpoint operator as desired, but the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate and D_out S D_in^{-1} are not stated.
S2.2 names subspaces from three-element subsets; nondegenerate labels in F^{tensor 3}, comparability on every edge and the central wires losing h are absent.
No step says P_V-P_U has rank dim V - dim U or that the N source edges have rank one.
S2.2's quote alludes to keeping the dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to N, but neither Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich nor s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b is given.
s<Wm is asserted, but the ratios L/N=100/539, 101/539 and the deficit N-2L>0 that produce it are absent.
'Frames cancelling so the endpoint operator is the desired one' alludes to it, but M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m and the shear H<-H+D on every role are not stated.

The factorization E_1 Pi E_2 is stated and S2.2/S2.3 speak of s smaller calls, but the plan says only 'cost scaling with rank', never that a rank-a shear is exactly a interchanges (recursive calls) plus O(V); conservative verdict.

S2.3 gives s calls on volume V/W, cost O(V e^tau) with tau=1-2^{-50}, and quotes that the deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}; the explicit recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau and log m<20 are left implicit.

central.summary: The plan asserts the outcome of the central saving (s<Wm, s calls on volume V/W, tau=1-2^{-50}) and the shear factorization, but not the mechanism that produces it: the network, frames and labels are only named, rank equals dimension change is absent, and the budget, the L/N ratios and the endpoint identity appear at most as allusions. Only the final recurrence step is reconstructed.
